source.text: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹראֱלֹהֵ֥י תְ֝הִלָּתִ֗י אַֽל־תֶּחֱרַֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director. Of David, a psalm. God of my praise, do not be silent.

en.L: For the director. Of David. A psalm. God of my praise, do not be silent.
en.B: For the music director. Of David. A psalm. God whom I praise, do not keep silent.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song by David. God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one I praise. Do not stay silent!

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: God of my praise: the God I praise
decisions.reason: God is the one the psalmist praises, the subject of all his praise (Deuteronomy 10:21). The psalm ends with that praise (verse 30).

decisions.choice: do not be silent: act, speak up for me
decisions.reason: God's silence is his not acting; the psalmist asks him to speak in his defense, as the liars speak against him (28:1; 83:2).

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

source.text: כִּ֤י פִ֪י רָשָׁ֡ע וּֽפִי־מִ֭רְמָה עָלַ֣י פָּתָ֑חוּ דִּבְּר֥וּ אִ֝תִּ֗י לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] mouth of [the] wicked and [the] mouth of deceit against me they have opened; they have spoken with me [with] a tongue of falsehood.

en.L: For [the] mouth of [the] wicked and [the] mouth of deceit they have opened against me; they have spoken with me [with] a tongue of falsehood.
en.B: For the wicked have opened deceitful mouths against me; they speak to me with lies on their tongues.
en.R: Evil people are attacking me with lies. Everything they say to me is false.

decisions.choice: opened a mouth against me: attacked with words
decisions.reason: The enemies' weapon is speech: lies, hatred and accusation (verses 2-5, 20, 29). The psalm asks God not to be silent while they speak.

decisions.choice: spoken with me: spoken to me, or against me
decisions.reason: The words ("with me") can mean speaking to him face to face, or speaking about him.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the prayer
decisions.reason: God must not stay silent because the liars are not silent.

source.text: וְדִבְרֵ֣י שִׂנְאָ֣ה סְבָב֑וּנִי וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֥וּנִי חִנָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [with] words of hatred they have surrounded me, and they have fought against me without cause.

en.L: And with words of hatred they have surrounded me, and they have fought against me without cause.
en.B: They have hemmed me in with hateful words and attacked me for no reason.
en.R: They surround me and say hateful things. They attack me, though I have done nothing to them.

decisions.choice: surrounded me: closed in like an army
decisions.reason: Their words are pictured as soldiers besieging him (22:13, 17).

decisions.choice: without cause: for nothing
decisions.reason: The word (chinnam) means free, for no reason: he gave them no cause (35:7; 69:5).

source.text: תַּֽחַת־אַהֲבָתִ֥י יִשְׂטְנ֗וּנִי וַאֲנִ֥י תְפִלָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In return for my love they accuse me, and I [am] prayer.

en.L: In return for my love they accuse me, but I [am] prayer.
en.B: They repay my love by accusing me, yet I go on praying.
en.R: I showed them love, but they accuse me in return. Even so, I keep praying.

decisions.choice: accuse me: act as my accuser
decisions.reason: The verb (satan) is to oppose as an adversary, especially in court. The same word comes as "accuser" in verses 6, 20 and 29: the psalm is a case at law.

decisions.choice: I am prayer: I give myself to prayer
decisions.reason: The short phrase ("and I prayer") means that all he does is pray, as 120:7 says "I am peace". It may also mean that he prays for them.

decisions.choice: I go on praying (B); I keep praying (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2).

source.text: וַיָּ֘שִׂ֤ימוּ עָלַ֣י רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה וְ֝שִׂנְאָ֗ה תַּ֣חַת אַהֲבָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they have put on me evil in place of good, and hatred in place of my love.

en.L: And they have laid on me evil in return for good, and hatred in return for my love.
en.B: They hand me evil for the good I did, and hatred in exchange for my love.
en.R: I did good to them, but they do evil to me. I loved them, but they hate me.

decisions.choice: laid on me: repaid me with
decisions.reason: The verb (sim) is to set or put: they have charged him with evil in return for good.

decisions.choice: evil for good
decisions.reason: The same complaint is made in 35:12 and 38:21. Returning evil for good is condemned in Proverbs 17:13.

source.text: הַפְקֵ֣ד עָלָ֣יו רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝שָׂטָ֗ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־יְמִינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Appoint over him a wicked [one], and let an accuser stand at his right hand.

en.L: Appoint over him a wicked [one], and let an accuser stand at his right hand.
en.B: Put someone wicked in charge of him; may an accuser take his stand at his right side.
en.R: Let an evil person be his judge. Let someone stand beside him in court to accuse him.

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment
decisions.reason: Verses 6-20 ask God to punish the accuser and to let his own curses fall on him. The psalmist does not take revenge himself; he has prayed (verse 4) and hands the case to God, the judge, asking for justice in God's court (Romans 12:19). The New Testament applies verse 8 to Judas (Acts 1:20).

decisions.choice: him: one enemy, or each of them
alternatives: verses 6-19 are the enemies' curses against the psalmist, quoted
decisions.reason: Verses 2-5 speak of the enemies as "they"; verses 6-19 speak of one man, perhaps their leader or each of them in turn. Some read verses 6-19 as the curses the enemies spoke against the psalmist, quoted by him; but the Hebrew gives no sign of a quotation, and verse 20 calls all this the wages of the accusers.

decisions.choice: an accuser: an opponent at law
decisions.reason: The word (satan) is an adversary, here an accuser in a trial (verse 4). In Zechariah 3:1 "the accuser" stands at the right hand of the high priest to accuse him. The ancient Greek translation has "the devil".

decisions.choice: at his right hand: the accuser's place in court
decisions.reason: In a trial the accuser stood at the right of the accused (Zechariah 3:1). In verse 31 it is God who stands at the right hand of the needy.

decisions.choice: Let an evil person be his judge
alternatives: Appoint a wicked one over him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of "appoint over him" in a trial.

source.text: בְּ֭הִשָּׁ֣פְטוֹ יֵצֵ֣א רָשָׁ֑ע וּ֝תְפִלָּת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַֽחֲטָאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and his prayer let it become sin.

en.L: When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and let his prayer become sin.
en.B: When he is tried, may the verdict be guilty, and may his very prayer count as sin.
en.R: When he goes on trial, let the court find him guilty. Let even his prayers count as sin.

decisions.choice: his prayer: his plea
decisions.reason: The word (tefillah) is prayer to God; here it may be his plea for mercy in court. Either way the plea of a guilty man who showed no mercy is to be refused.

decisions.choice: come out guilty: leave the court condemned
decisions.reason: To "come out" of a trial is to be declared guilty or innocent (17:2).

source.text: יִֽהְיֽוּ־יָמָ֥יו מְעַטִּ֑ים פְּ֝קֻדָּת֗וֹ יִקַּ֥ח אַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Let his days be few; his office let another take.

en.L: Let his days be few; let another take his office.
en.B: May his life be short, and may someone else take over his position.
en.R: Let his life be cut short. Let someone else take over his place as a leader.

decisions.choice: Acts 1:20: another takes Judas's place
decisions.reason: Peter quotes this line, with 69:26, of Judas after his death, and the apostles choose Matthias to take his place (Acts 1:20-26).

decisions.choice: his office: his post of oversight
decisions.reason: The word (pequddah) is an appointed charge or office (Numbers 4:16). It can also mean goods in someone's care.

decisions.choice: his days be few: may he die early
decisions.reason: A short life was a sign of judgment (55:24).

source.text: יִֽהְיוּ־בָנָ֥יו יְתוֹמִ֑ים וְ֝אִשְׁתּוֹ אַלְמָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.

en.L: Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
en.B: May his children lose their father and his wife be left a widow.
en.R: Let his children be left without a father, and let his wife become a widow.

decisions.choice: his family shares his fate
decisions.reason: A man's household stood or fell with him (Exodus 20:5; Joshua 7:24). He made others poor and helpless (verse 16); the prayer is that he and his receive the same.

source.text: וְנ֤וֹעַ יָנ֣וּעוּ בָנָ֣יו וְשִׁאֵ֑לוּ וְ֝דָרְשׁ֗וּ מֵחָרְבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And wandering let them wander, his children, and let them beg, and let them seek [food] from their ruins.

en.L: And let his children wander and wander, and beg, and seek [food] from their ruins.
en.B: May his children roam about as beggars, searching for food far from their ruined homes.
en.R: Let his children wander from place to place, begging. Let them search for food far from the ruins of their homes.

decisions.choice: wander and wander: always on the move
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: they will wander without rest, like Cain (Genesis 4:12).

decisions.choice: seek from their ruins: search for food away from home
alternatives: let them be driven out of their ruins (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "let them seek from their ruins". The ancient Greek translation read a word very like it, "let them be driven out". Both describe children forced out of a ruined home to beg.

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: What beggars seek is food; Literal brackets it.

source.text: יְנַקֵּ֣שׁ נ֭וֹשֶׁה לְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְיָבֹ֖זּוּ זָרִ֣ים יְגִיעֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let a creditor ensnare all that [belongs] to him, and let strangers plunder his labor.

en.L: Let the creditor seize all that [belongs] to him, and let strangers plunder [the fruit of] his toil.
en.B: May the moneylender snatch up all he owns, and strangers carry off what he worked for.
en.R: Let the people he owes money to take everything he has. Let strangers steal all he worked for.

decisions.choice: let the creditor seize: lay hold of, as in a trap
decisions.reason: The verb (naqash) is to lay a snare; the creditor (nosheh) is one who has lent and now takes everything in payment (2 Kings 4:1).

decisions.choice: his labor: what he has worked for
decisions.reason: The word (yegia') is toil and what it produces (128:2).

source.text: אַל־יְהִי־ל֭וֹמֹשֵׁ֣ךְ חָ֑סֶד וְֽאַל־יְהִ֥י ח֝וֹנֵ֗ן לִיתוֹמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Let there not be to him one who extends loyal love, and let there not be one who shows favor to his fatherless [children].

en.L: Let there be no one to extend loyal love to him, and let there be no one to show favor to his fatherless [children].
en.B: May no one keep showing him loyal love, and no one take pity on his orphaned children.
en.R: Let no one be kind to him. Let no one care for his children when they have no father.

decisions.choice: extend loyal love: keep up kindness
decisions.reason: Loyal love (chesed) is here the faithful kindness people owe each other. He did not remember to show it (verse 16), and the prayer is that none be shown to him. To "extend" (mashakh) is to draw it out, to keep it going (36:11).

decisions.choice: be kind
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for loyal love between people.

source.text: יְהִֽי־אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית בְּד֥וֹר אַ֝חֵ֗ר יִמַּ֥ח שְׁמָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let his posterity be for cutting off; in another generation let their name be wiped out.

en.L: Let his posterity be for cutting off; in another generation let their name be blotted out.
en.B: May his line come to an end, their name erased within a generation.
en.R: Let his family line end, so that in the next generation no one is left to carry their name.

decisions.choice: their name wiped out: the family dies out
decisions.reason: A family's name lived on in its sons; to have it wiped out was the worst loss (Deuteronomy 25:6). "Their" is the name of his descendants.

decisions.choice: posterity: those who come after
decisions.reason: The word ('acharit) is the end or what comes after: his descendants, his future (37:37-38).

source.text: יִזָּכֵ֤ר׀עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וְחַטַּ֥את אִ֝מּ֗וֹ אַל־תִּמָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered to YHWH, and the sin of his mother let it not be wiped out.

en.L: Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep in mind the guilt of his ancestors, and may his mother's sin never be erased.
en.R: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remember the wrong his ancestors did, and never forget his mother's sin.

decisions.choice: the sins of the parents
decisions.reason: The prayer asks God to hold the family's guilt against the man, as the law warns for those who hate God (Exodus 20:5). Elsewhere each person bears his own sin (Ezekiel 18:20); here the psalmist leaves the judgment to God.

decisions.choice: remembered to the LORD: kept before him
decisions.reason: For God to remember sin is for him to act on it; for him to wipe it out is to forgive (51:3).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The fathers are the forebears of the family.

source.text: יִהְי֣וּ נֶֽגֶד־יְהוָ֣ה תָּמִ֑יד וְיַכְרֵ֖ת מֵאֶ֣רֶץ זִכְרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them be before YHWH continually, and let him cut off from [the] earth their memory.

en.L: Let them be before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually, and may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cut off their memory from the earth.
en.B: May their sins stay always before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
en.R: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} always keep their sins in mind, and let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} make the whole world forget them.

decisions.choice: them: the sins of verse 14
decisions.reason: "Let them be before the LORD" refers to the iniquity and sin of verse 14. "Their memory" is that of the man and his family.

decisions.choice: cut off their memory: 34:17
decisions.reason: The same words are used of evildoers in 34:17.

decisions.choice: their sins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "them" refers to (m1).

source.text: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר׀לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ עֲשׂ֪וֹת חָ֥סֶד וַיִּרְדֹּ֡ף אִישׁ־עָנִ֣י וְ֭אֶבְיוֹן וְנִכְאֵ֨ה לֵבָ֬ב לְמוֹתֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Because that he did not remember to do loyal love, and he pursued a poor and needy man and [the] disheartened of heart, to put [them] to death.

en.L: Because he did not remember to do loyal love, and he pursued a poor and needy {{gender:person|man}} and the crushed of heart, to put [them] to death.
en.B: For he never thought to show loyal love; he hounded the poor and needy and the heartbroken to their death.
en.R: He never cared about being kind. Instead he hunted down poor people who needed help and people whose hearts were broken, wanting to kill them.

decisions.choice: the reason: he showed no loyal love
decisions.reason: The judgment fits the deed. He showed no loyal love (chesed), so none is to be shown to him (verse 12); he loved cursing, so cursing comes to him (verse 17).

decisions.choice: disheartened of heart: crushed in spirit
decisions.reason: The word (nikh'eh) is broken or crushed; with "heart" it is someone whose spirit is crushed. The psalmist is himself "poor and needy" (verse 22).

decisions.choice: person (man)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "man" ('ish) here means anyone poor; the default says "person", with "man" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: being kind
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב קְ֭לָלָה וַתְּבוֹאֵ֑הוּ וְֽלֹא־חָפֵ֥ץ בִּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה וַתִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he loved cursing, and it came to him; and he did not delight in blessing, and it was far from him.

en.L: And he loved cursing, and it came to him; and he did not delight in blessing, and it was far from him.
en.B: He loved to curse, and the curse has come back on him; he had no wish to bless, and blessing has stayed far from him.
en.R: He loved to curse others, and now curses fall on him. He never wanted to bless anyone, and now no blessing comes to him.

decisions.choice: it came, it was far: what has happened to him
alternatives: let it come to him; let it be far from him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs say what has happened: the curse came, the blessing stayed away. The ancient translations read them as wishes, "let it come ... let it be far", continuing the prayer.

decisions.choice: curse and blessing return to the one who speaks them
decisions.reason: What he wished on others comes back on him (7:16-17; Proverbs 26:27). God promised Abraham to bless those who bless him and curse those who curse him (Genesis 12:3).

source.text: וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ קְלָלָ֗ה כְּמַ֫דּ֥וֹ וַתָּבֹ֣א כַמַּ֣יִם בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְ֝כַשֶּׁ֗מֶן בְּעַצְמוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put on cursing like his garment, and it came like water into his inner parts, and like oil into his bones.

en.L: And he clothed himself with cursing like his garment, and it came like water into his inner parts, and like oil into his bones.
en.B: He put on cursing as his clothing; it seeped like water into his inner being and soaked like oil deep into his bones.
en.R: Cursing was part of him, like the clothes he wore. It filled him the way water soaks in, the way oil sinks deep into the bones.

decisions.choice: put on cursing like a garment: it became part of him
decisions.reason: What a person wears shows what he is (35:26; 73:6). Cursing was as close to him as his clothes.

decisions.choice: like oil into his bones: soaking right through
decisions.reason: Oil rubbed on the skin sinks in. The curse he loved has filled him through and through.

decisions.choice: it came: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the verbs say what has happened; the ancient translations read them as wishes.

source.text: תְּהִי־ל֭וֹכְּבֶ֣גֶד יַעְטֶ֑ה וּ֝לְמֵ֗זַח תָּמִ֥יד יַחְגְּרֶֽהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let it be to him like a garment [that] he wraps himself, and for a belt [that] continually he girds on.

en.L: Let it be to him like a garment [that] he wraps around himself, and like a belt [that] he continually ties on.
en.B: May it be the cloak he wraps around him, the belt he ties on every day.
en.R: Let his curses cover him like a coat and stay tied around him like a belt he never takes off.

decisions.choice: let it be: the cursing of verse 18
decisions.reason: The cursing he put on is to stay on him for good.

decisions.choice: belt: a waistband
decisions.reason: The word (meziach) is a belt or sash, worn every day and seldom taken off.

decisions.choice: his curses
decisions.reason: Readable says what "it" is (m1).

source.text: זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְהַדֹּבְרִ֥ים רָ֝֗ע עַל־נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] wages of my accusers from YHWH, and of those who speak evil against my soul.

en.L: This [is] the wages of my accusers from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and of those who speak evil against my soul.
en.B: May this be how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repays my accusers, those who speak evil against me.
en.R: Let this be the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pays back the people who accuse me and tell evil lies about me.

decisions.choice: this: all of verses 6-19
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the prayer for judgment: this is to be the pay the accusers receive from the LORD. It ends the section on judgment (verses 6-20).

decisions.choice: wages: what is earned
decisions.reason: The word (pe'ullah) is the pay for work done; they will receive what their deeds have earned.

decisions.choice: my accusers
decisions.reason: The same word (satan) as in verses 4 and 6.

decisions.choice: against me
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) is the whole self; Balanced and Readable say "me".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֤ה׀יְה֘וִ֤ה אֲדֹנָ֗י עֲֽשֵׂה־אִ֭תִּי לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּי־ט֥וֹב חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ הַצִּילֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, YHWH [the] Lord, act with me for [the] sake of your name; for good [is] your loyal love, deliver me.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my Lord, deal with me for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love [is] good, deliver me.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, take my side for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; rescue me, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love is good.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, help me, so that people will honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. Your faithful love is good, so rescue me!

decisions.choice: but you: the prayer turns
decisions.reason: After the prayer for judgment, the psalmist turns to God for himself. The stressed "you" sets God against the accusers.

decisions.choice: YHWH the Lord: the name with 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The name comes first, then "my Lord" ('Adonai), as in 68:21 and 140:8.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord (L); Lord GOD (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 68:21: where the name stands with "Lord", it is written GOD so that the two are not read as "Lord Lord"; Balanced and Readable use the familiar order.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your name: for your honor
decisions.reason: God's name is his known character; to act for its sake is to act so that he is known as faithful (23:3; 79:9).

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 107:1.

decisions.choice: so that people will honor your name
alternatives: for the sake of your name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m4).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

source.text: כִּֽי־עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֣וֹן אָנֹ֑כִי וְ֝לִבִּ֗י חָלַ֥ל בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For poor and needy [am] I, and my heart is pierced within me.

en.L: For poor and needy [am] I, and my heart is pierced within me.
en.B: For I am poor and helpless; my heart within me is pierced through.
en.R: I am poor, and I need help. My heart is broken and full of pain.

decisions.choice: poor and needy: the one the enemy hunted
decisions.reason: The psalmist is the "poor and needy" whom the enemy pursued to death (verse 16).

decisions.choice: pierced: wounded
decisions.reason: The verb (chalal) is to pierce or wound: grief and hurt have stabbed him to the heart.

decisions.choice: my heart is broken and full of pain
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

source.text: כְּצֵל־כִּנְטוֹת֥וֹ נֶהֱלָ֑כְתִּי נִ֝נְעַ֗רְתִּי כָּֽאַרְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a shadow when it stretches out I have gone; I have been shaken off like the locust.

en.L: Like a shadow when it stretches out, I have gone; I have been shaken off like the locust.
en.B: Like a shadow lengthening at dusk I pass away; I am brushed off like a locust.
en.R: I am disappearing like a shadow at the end of the day. People shake me off like a locust on their clothes.

decisions.choice: a shadow when it stretches out: evening coming on
decisions.reason: A long shadow means the day is ending; soon it will vanish. The picture is of a life near its end (102:12; 144:4).

decisions.choice: shaken off like a locust: brushed off as worthless
decisions.reason: A locust that lands on clothing is shaken off without a thought; locusts were also swept away by the wind (Exodus 10:19).

decisions.choice: People; on their clothes
decisions.reason: Readable says who shakes him off and from where (m2).

source.text: בִּ֭רְכַּי כָּשְׁל֣וּ מִצּ֑וֹם וּ֝בְשָׂרִ֗י כָּחַ֥שׁ מִשָּֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: My knees have stumbled from fasting, and my flesh has grown lean from fat.

en.L: My knees have stumbled from fasting, and my flesh has grown lean, without fat.
en.B: My knees buckle from going without food, and my body has grown thin, with no fat left on it.
en.R: I have gone without food for so long that my knees are weak. I have become skin and bones.

decisions.choice: fasting: going without food in grief and prayer
decisions.reason: People fasted when they mourned or prayed in great need (35:13; 69:11).

decisions.choice: lean from fat: wasted away
decisions.reason: The words mean his body has lost its fat. They may also mean "without oil": he has not anointed himself, as mourners did not (2 Samuel 14:2).

decisions.choice: I have become skin and bones
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain picture with the same sense.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י׀הָיִ֣יתִי חֶרְפָּ֣ה לָהֶ֑ם יִ֝רְא֗וּנִי יְנִיע֥וּן רֹאשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have become a reproach to them; they see me, they shake their head.

en.L: And I have become a reproach to them; they see me, they shake their head.
en.B: They treat me with contempt; when they catch sight of me, they shake their heads at me.
en.R: People laugh at me. They see me and shake their heads to mock me.

decisions.choice: shake the head: mock
decisions.reason: Shaking the head was a gesture of scorn (22:8; 44:15). Those who passed by the cross shook their heads at Jesus (Matthew 27:39).

decisions.choice: a reproach: one who is scorned
decisions.reason: The word (cherpah) is disgrace, and a person treated with contempt (22:7).

decisions.choice: They treat me with contempt (B); People laugh at me (R)
alternatives: I have become a reproach to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say it from the side of those who scorn him.

source.text: עָ֭זְרֵנִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י ה֭וֹשִׁיעֵ֣נִי כְחַסְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Help me, YHWH my God; save me according to your loyal love.

en.L: Help me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God; save me according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, come to my help! Save me, true to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, help me! Save me, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love promises.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 107:1 and verse 21.

decisions.choice: according to your loyal love: as your love would do
decisions.reason: God's loyal love is the measure of his help, and the ground of the plea.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

source.text: וְֽ֭יֵדְעוּ כִּי־יָ֣דְךָ זֹּ֑את אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה עֲשִׂיתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And let them know that your hand [is] this; you, YHWH, you have done it.

en.L: And let them know that this [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have done it.
en.B: Make them see that this is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hand at work, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are the one who did it.
en.R: Then my enemies will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did this, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. They will see that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power saved me.

decisions.choice: your hand: your power at work
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and action (107:2). His rescue is to be so plain that the enemies see God did it.

decisions.choice: you, you have done it: stressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun is repeated: it is God and no one else who acted.

decisions.choice: my enemies; saved me
decisions.reason: Readable names who will know and what God's hand did.

source.text: יְקַֽלְלוּ־הֵמָּה֮ וְאַתָּ֪ה תְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ קָ֤מוּ׀וַיֵּבֹ֗שׁוּ וְֽעַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשְׂמָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them curse, they, but you will bless; they have arisen and been shamed, but your servant will rejoice.

en.L: Let them curse, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bless; they have risen up and been put to shame, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant will rejoice.
en.B: They may curse, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bless; when they rise against me they will be disgraced, while {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant rejoices.
en.R: They may curse me, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bless me. They attack me, but they will end up ashamed, and I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, will be glad.

decisions.choice: they curse, you bless
decisions.reason: The key words of verses 17-18 come back: human curses cannot stand against God's blessing (Numbers 23:8; Genesis 12:3).

decisions.choice: they have arisen and been shamed: as good as done
alternatives: let those who rise against me be put to shame (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The verbs are past in form, but they describe what is sure to happen: when they rise up, they will be put to shame. The ancient Greek translation reads a wish.

decisions.choice: when they rise against me they will be disgraced (B); they will end up ashamed (R)
alternatives: they have arisen and been ashamed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the verbs (m2).

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they curse and God blesses.

source.text: יִלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שׂוֹטְנַ֣י כְּלִמָּ֑ה וְיַעֲט֖וּ כַמְעִ֣יל בָּשְׁתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let my accusers be clothed [with] disgrace, and let them wrap themselves like the robe [in] their shame.

en.L: Let my accusers be clothed [with] disgrace, and let them wrap themselves in their shame as [in] a robe.
en.B: May my accusers be dressed in dishonor and wrapped in their own shame like a cloak.
en.R: Let the people who accuse me be covered with disgrace. Let their shame wrap around them like a coat.

decisions.choice: clothed with shame: the cursing they wore
decisions.reason: As the enemy put on cursing like a garment (verses 18-19), the accusers are to wear their own shame (35:26).

decisions.choice: my accusers
decisions.reason: The same word (satan) as in verses 4, 6 and 20.

source.text: א֘וֹדֶ֤ה יְהוָ֣ה מְאֹ֣ד בְּפִ֑י וּבְת֖וֹךְ רַבִּ֣ים אֲהַֽלְלֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will thank YHWH exceedingly with my mouth, and in [the] midst of many I will praise him.

en.L: I will thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} exceedingly with my mouth, and in the midst of many I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: My lips will thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} over and over; I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the middle of the crowd.
en.R: I will thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} out loud, again and again. I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in front of many people.

decisions.choice: in the midst of many: thanks in public
decisions.reason: Thanks for a rescue was given aloud before the gathered people (22:23, 26; 35:18).

decisions.choice: exceedingly: greatly, fully
decisions.reason: The word (me'od) makes the thanks great and wholehearted.

decisions.choice: my lips
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the more natural picture for speaking praise.

source.text: כִּֽי־יַ֭עֲמֹד לִימִ֣ין אֶבְי֑וֹן לְ֝הוֹשִׁ֗יעַ מִשֹּׁפְטֵ֥י נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For he stands at [the] right hand of [the] needy, to save [him] from those who judge his soul.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stands at the right hand of the needy, to save [{{gender:them|him}}] from those who judge {{gender:their|his}} soul.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the right side of the needy, to save them from those who would sentence them to death.
en.R: He stands right beside people in need. He saves them from those who want them condemned to death.

decisions.choice: at the right hand of the needy: the defender's place
decisions.reason: The accuser stood at the right hand of the accused (verse 6). Here God himself stands at the right hand of the needy as defender, and the case turns.

decisions.choice: those who judge his soul: those who condemn him to death
decisions.reason: To judge someone's soul (nefesh) is to pass sentence on his life.

decisions.choice: them, their (him, his)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the needy as "him"; the default says "them", with "him" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: the needy ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of the needy as a group, which includes men and women alike.
